ideas.hypothesis: The share of geotagged social media posts in a city made by foreign residents and visitors can serve as a high-frequency, city-level globalization index. It should track trade, foreign investment and air passenger links and predict local economic globalization better than national indices.
ideas.test: Collect geotagged posts for about 100 cities over several years and classify users as foreign or local by language and posting history. Correlate the foreign-user share with city-level international air passengers, foreign affiliate employment and export data, and test whether it predicts these better than national globalization indices.
ideas.disconfirming: The geotag-based index is uncorrelated with, or adds nothing to national indices in predicting, city-level trade, investment and air-link measures.

ideas.hypothesis: If the track-and-field decomposition is replicated with data extended to 2019 and applied to another sport (swimming), technological progress will still dominate globalization (a wider pool of competing countries) in explaining record improvements.
ideas.test: Collect annual best performances and the number of competing nations for athletics events up to 2019 and for long-course swimming. Re-estimate the original decomposition and compare the shares attributed to globalization and to technology.
ideas.disconfirming: In the extended or swimming data, the globalization component explains a larger share of record improvement than technological progress.

ideas.hypothesis: Internet access spreads training knowledge, so its diffusion speeds up improvement in national athletic performance in late-adopting countries and narrows their gap to the leading nations.
ideas.test: Build a country-year panel of national record or season-best performances by event, merged with internet penetration rates for 1990-2019. Estimate convergence regressions of the performance gap to world-leading levels on lagged internet penetration, with country and event fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Internet diffusion does not predict faster performance convergence once participation and income are controlled for.

ideas.hypothesis: Countries that hire foreign coaches improve athletic performance faster than countries with similar participation, implying that globalization works through knowledge transfer as well as through new competitors entering.
ideas.test: Use national federation records of head-coach nationality by event group, merged with country-event performance panels. Estimate event-study models around the arrival of a foreign coach.
ideas.disconfirming: Performance trends do not change after a foreign coach arrives, compared with matched countries.

ideas.hypothesis: The entry of athletes from BRIC countries after 1990 accounts for a measurable share of top-level performance improvement in distance events, consistent with globalization widening the competitor pool.
ideas.test: Use annual top-100 performance lists with athlete nationality for 1980-2019. Build counterfactual top-performance series that exclude BRIC athletes and compare improvement rates.
ideas.disconfirming: Excluding BRIC athletes leaves the rate of top-performance improvement essentially unchanged.

ideas.hypothesis: Moldovan SMEs that face weaker contract enforcement report bigger globalization challenges and export less, because cross-border relationships depend on enforceable contracts.
ideas.test: Use firm-level enterprise survey data for Moldova and neighbouring transition economies with questions on court effectiveness and dispute resolution. Estimate probits of export participation and reported globalization obstacles on perceived contract enforcement.
ideas.disconfirming: Perceived contract enforcement has no association with SME export participation or reported globalization challenges.

ideas.hypothesis: More frequent face-to-face interaction between multinational headquarters and subsidiaries, made easier by new direct flight routes, raises knowledge transfer and subsidiary productivity.
ideas.test: Treat the opening of new direct air routes between headquarters and subsidiary cities as shocks. Run a difference-in-differences on subsidiary total factor productivity from firm financial databases, comparing affected and unaffected subsidiary-headquarters pairs.
ideas.disconfirming: Subsidiary productivity does not change after the new direct links open.

ideas.hypothesis: Metro areas more integrated into global capital markets (higher foreign buyer shares) see larger declines in housing affordability for local first-time buyers and more permanent renting.
ideas.test: Use Australian metro or local-area data on foreign residential investment approvals merged with price-to-income ratios and tenure shares for 2005-2019. Run panel regressions with instruments based on source-country wealth shocks.
ideas.disconfirming: Local foreign-buyer intensity is unrelated to affordability and tenure outcomes.

ideas.hypothesis: Expansions of major central banks' balance sheets spill over more strongly to domestic bank lending in more globalized economies.
ideas.test: Use a quarterly cross-country panel of domestic credit growth regressed on changes in the Fed and ECB balance sheets, interacted with a composite economic globalization index and controls for domestic policy rates.
ideas.disconfirming: The interaction between foreign balance sheet expansion and globalization is zero.

ideas.hypothesis: Large foreign acquisitions of agricultural land go disproportionately to countries with weak contract enforcement and insecure land tenure, where land is cheap and local claims are easy to override.
ideas.test: Estimate a gravity-style count model of transnational land deals (from a public land-deal database) on target-country contract-enforcement indicators, controlling for land availability, yields and distance.
ideas.disconfirming: Deals concentrate in countries with stronger contract enforcement, or enforcement has no effect.

ideas.hypothesis: Greater economic globalization lowers defense spending as a share of GDP, because integration raises the opportunity cost of conflict, unless the country faces high regional threat levels.
ideas.test: Use a country panel of military expenditure shares from the extended SIPRI data, regressed on a globalization index with an interaction for regional conflict intensity, instrumented by trade-cost shocks.
ideas.disconfirming: Defense spending shares rise with economic globalization or are unrelated to it.

ideas.hypothesis: Multinational regional offices prefer transit-oriented districts with high accessibility, so new transit-oriented development raises the probability that a multinational locates an office nearby.
ideas.test: Geocode multinational office openings in several metros and run a difference-in-differences comparing station areas that received transit-oriented development with matched station areas that did not.
ideas.disconfirming: Multinational office location does not change after transit-oriented development.

ideas.hypothesis: Workers displaced by import competition are reemployed faster in metros where public transit gives better access to employment, so transport accessibility softens the local costs of globalization.
ideas.test: Link displaced-worker survey records or administrative unemployment spells to tract-level transit job-access measures. Estimate reemployment hazards for trade-displaced workers by access level.
ideas.disconfirming: Transit job access does not predict reemployment speed for trade-displaced workers.

ideas.hypothesis: Valuation uncertainty, measured as the gap between valuation and transaction price, is larger in property markets with a high share of foreign buyers, because foreign demand adds intangible uncertainty.
ideas.test: Use transaction-level data with pre-sale valuations and buyer residency flags. Regress the absolute valuation error on local foreign-buyer share, controlling for property characteristics.
ideas.disconfirming: Valuation errors are equal or smaller in markets with high foreign-buyer shares.

ideas.hypothesis: Urban spaces where geotagged posts show foreign visitors and locals in the same places act as cultural exchange hotspots, and cities with more of them later see larger growth in inbound tourism and services trade.
ideas.test: Identify co-presence hotspots from geotagged posts with language detection in a sample of cities. Regress later changes in tourist arrivals and services exports on baseline hotspot density.
ideas.disconfirming: Hotspot density does not predict later growth in tourism or services trade.

ideas.hypothesis: Multinational branch plants attracted by regional policy subsidies close more often in recessions than comparable domestic plants, so subsidy-led regional globalization is less resilient.
ideas.test: Run plant-level survival analysis in Ireland or the UK comparing subsidized foreign plants, unsubsidized foreign plants and domestic plants across the 2008-2010 recession.
ideas.disconfirming: Subsidized multinational plants are no more likely to close in recessions than domestic plants.

ideas.hypothesis: As New Zealand's economy globalized, the New Zealand stock market's returns moved more closely with global equity returns, reducing diversification benefits for local investors.
ideas.test: Estimate dynamic conditional correlations between New Zealand index returns and a world equity index for 1990-2019, then regress the correlations on New Zealand's trade and investment openness measures.
ideas.disconfirming: Return co-movement does not rise with New Zealand's globalization measures.

ideas.hypothesis: When multinational ride-hailing platforms enter a city, local taxi trips and driver earnings fall more in cities where public transport is weaker.
ideas.test: Run a staggered difference-in-differences on platform entry across cities using taxi trip records or licensing data, interacted with baseline public transport supply.
ideas.disconfirming: Taxi trips and earnings do not fall after entry, or the drop does not depend on transit quality.

ideas.hypothesis: Moldovan SMEs that adopt e-commerce and electronic payment are more likely to export, which eases the globalization challenges they report.
ideas.test: Survey Moldovan SMEs on electronic payment and online sales adoption and export status. Estimate probits with an instrument such as local bank digital-service rollout.
ideas.disconfirming: E-commerce adoption has no association with exporting once firm size and sector are controlled for.

ideas.hypothesis: Moldova's low economic complexity limits SMEs' integration into global value chains. Products that are closer in product space to Moldova's existing capabilities show faster export growth.
ideas.test: Use product-level export data for Moldova for 2000-2019 to compute product-space density for each product, and regress later export growth or new export entry on density.
ideas.disconfirming: Density does not predict export growth or entry of new products.

ideas.hypothesis: Highway project selection that models freight demand as stochastic and driven by trade shocks delivers better system performance in trade-exposed corridors than deterministic selection.
ideas.test: Backtest the stochastic optimization model on a state agency's historical project portfolio, with freight scenarios drawn from observed trade volatility. Compare realized performance under the stochastic and deterministic selections.
ideas.disconfirming: The stochastic selection performs no better than the deterministic one in trade-exposed corridors.

ideas.hypothesis: Travel demand forecast errors are larger in regions with high exposure to globalization (port- and trade-dependent employment), because standard forecasts leave out trade shocks.
ideas.test: Compile forecast and actual traffic for completed road projects and regress absolute percentage forecast errors on the regional trade-exposed employment share.
ideas.disconfirming: Forecast errors are unrelated to regional globalization exposure.

ideas.hypothesis: Field surveys of SMEs about globalization challenges over-sample surviving firms and so understate the negative effects of globalization. Reweighting with business registry exit data increases the measured challenges.
ideas.test: Link a survey sample to business registry entry and exit records, estimate selection with a Heckman correction or inverse-probability weights, and compare corrected and uncorrected challenge scores.
ideas.disconfirming: Corrected and uncorrected estimates of globalization challenges are essentially identical.

ideas.hypothesis: A validated scale of perceived globalization challenges for SMEs will show distinct factors (market access, finance, regulation, culture), each predicting export behaviour differently.
ideas.test: Pilot a Likert questionnaire with about 300 SMEs, run exploratory and confirmatory factor analysis, and test predictive validity against export status one year later.
ideas.disconfirming: A single factor fits as well as the multi-factor model, or the subscales do not predict exporting.

ideas.hypothesis: Surcharges and stamp duties on foreign buyers raise the market share of local first-time home buyers in the affected housing markets.
ideas.test: Run a difference-in-differences on foreign-buyer tax introductions (e.g., Vancouver 2016, Auckland 2018), comparing first-time buyer shares in treated and untreated markets using land-registry or mortgage data.
ideas.disconfirming: First-time buyer shares do not rise in treated markets relative to controls.

ideas.hypothesis: Regions with stronger international social connectedness (friendship links measured from social network data) have higher bilateral trade and foreign investment, even after controlling for distance and common language.
ideas.test: Estimate a gravity model of bilateral trade and investment between region or country pairs on a social connectedness index, with origin and destination fixed effects.
ideas.disconfirming: Social connectedness is insignificant once distance and standard gravity controls are included.

ideas.hypothesis: In the literature on globalization and growth, studies with stronger methods (instrumental variables, panel fixed effects) report smaller growth effects of globalization than cross-sectional studies.
ideas.test: Collect published estimates of globalization's effect on growth, code methodological quality, and run a meta-regression with publication-bias corrections.
ideas.disconfirming: Methodological quality is unrelated to the size of the estimated globalization effect.

ideas.hypothesis: Big data from satellite ship tracking (port calls) nowcasts bilateral trade flows more accurately than traditional indicators, especially for small economies whose statistics are slow to appear.
ideas.test: Aggregate vessel port-call data by country pair and month, then compare out-of-sample nowcasts of official trade with and without the ship-tracking predictors.
ideas.disconfirming: Ship-tracking predictors do not reduce nowcast errors relative to traditional indicators.

ideas.hypothesis: Stricter data privacy regimes reduce cross-border digital services trade with partner countries that lack data-adequacy agreements.
ideas.test: Estimate a gravity model of bilateral digital services trade, using the timing of a major privacy regulation and of adequacy decisions as treatment variation.
ideas.disconfirming: Digital services trade with non-adequate partners does not fall after privacy regimes tighten.

ideas.hypothesis: Multinational presence speeds up new industrialization (a rising high-tech manufacturing share) in small peripheral economies only when multinationals build domestic supplier linkages. Without those linkages, growth is a mirage, with weak social outcomes.
ideas.test: Use a country or region panel of multinational affiliate output, domestic sourcing shares from input-output tables, and high-tech manufacturing shares, and regress industrialization on affiliate presence interacted with linkages.
ideas.disconfirming: Multinational presence raises high-tech industrialization equally with or without domestic linkages, or not at all.
